 Ps. Badarpur

 Judgment
Part A - The lis at a glance A.
Serial No. of the Case: 182/21 B.
Date of Commission: 06.11.2020 C.

Name of the Complainant: HC Santosh Kumar No. 2006/SE D. Name of Accused: Raghvendra R.
S/o. Sh.
Ramasamy, R/o. H. No. 2494/65, MolarbandExtension, Badarpur, New Delhi.
E. Offence complained of: 283 IPC F. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty.

G. Final Order: Convicted H. Date of such order: 11.01.2021 I. Date of Institution of Case: 11.01.2021 Part B - A brief statement of reasons for the decision (As mandated u/s 355(i) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.)

BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION:
1.

The case of the prosecution is that on 06.11.2020 at about 5.00 P.M. at IInd 60 Foota Road,
Molarband Extension, New Delhi, within the jurisdiction of P.S. Badarpur, which was a public way,
accused Raghvendra R. (hereinafter, referred to as "the accused") had stationed his 'rehdi/rehri' on road for selling South Indian Food under the name and style of 'South Indian Masala Dosa' (Ravi Madrasi) and caused obstruction in the public way and thus, committed offence punishable u/s. 283 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter, to be referred as 'IPC').
2.
After investigation, chargesheet was filed on 11.01.2021.
The Court took cognizance of offence.

Documents were furnished to the accused under section 207 of Criminal Procedure Code,
(hereinafter, referred to as Cr.PC).
3.
Since the Court was of primafacie view that offence punishable under Sections 283 of IPC was made out against the accused, notice u/s. 251 of Cr.P.C. was served upon the accused for the said offence.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Since the witness was present before the State vs . Raghvendra R. on 11 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79563241/
1 Court, it proceeded to record evidence in the matter.
PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4.
The prosecution examined one witness in support of its case.

PW1 HC Santosh Kumar deposed that on 06.11.2020, he was posted as Head Constable at PS Badarpur and on that day, he was on patrolling duty from 05.00 pm to 11.00 pm in the area of Molarband Extension, Badarpur, New Delhi.

He further deposed that at about 5.00 pm, while he alongwith Constable Manish was at IInd 60 Foota Road, Molarband Extension, they saw one person, who had stationed his 'rehdi/rehri' on road for selling South Indian Food under the name and style of 'South Indian Masala Dosa' (Ravi Madarasi).
Due to this act, the commuters / passerby were having obstruction in their movement.
He clicked the photographs of the shop, which are MarkP (Colly.).
Further, he deposed that he prepared tehrir, which is Ex.PW1/A under his signatures and handed over the same to Ct. Manish for getting the FIR registered.
Thereafter, Ct. Manish got the FIR registered from the PS and returned with the copy of FIR along with original tehrir and handed over the same to the witness.
He further deposed that the accused was arrested at the spot vide arrest memo Ex. PW1/B, which bears his signature at point A.
Accused was released on police bail.
The site plan was prepared at the spot by him and the same is Ex.PW1/C, bearing his signature at point 'A'.
Witness was duly cross examined.
5. Vide a separate statement, accused admitted the genuineness of following document (without admitting the contents thereof):

(a). FIR No. 518/2020, PS Badarpur with certificate u/s.65B of Indian Evidence Act as Ex. A1 (Colly.).
6.
Prosecution evidence was closed and statement of accused u/s. 313 Cr.P.C read with Section 281 Cr.P.C was recorded, wherein he denied the incriminating evidence against him.
He stated that he did not wish to lead defence evidence.
7. Final arguments were heard.
This Court has given its thoughtful consideration to the material on record and submissions made by Ld. APP for State and Ld. Defence Counsel.
REASONING 8.

To bring home the guilt of the accused under section 283 IPC, the prosecution is required to establish the following essential ingredients beyond reasonable doubt:
(i) that the accused did an act or ommitted to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge.
(ii) that such act or omission caused danger / obstruction / injury to any person in any public way or line of navigation.

sentences.text: It is a settled legal proposition that in a criminal trial, prosecution has to stand on his own legs and prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

In Latesh @ Dadu Babu Rao Karlekar vs. State of Maharashtra (2018) 3SCC 66 "reasonable doubt" has been enunciated by Hon'ble Apex Court as a mean between excessive caution and excessive indifference to a doubt.

entities.text: Latesh @ Dadu Babu Rao Karlekar vs. State of Maharashtra (2018) 3SCC 66
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, it has been elaborated that reasonable doubt must be a practical one and not an abstract theoretical hypothesis.
While proving its case on the statutory standard, prosecution cannot rely upon the discrepancies in the case of accused /defence.

Reliance is placed upon Anand Ramachandra Chougala Vs. Sidarai Laxman Chougala & Ors. (Crl. Appl. No.1006/2010) and State of Karnataka Vs. Sidarai Laxman Chougala & Ors. (Crl. Appeal No. 1007/2010) decided by the Apex Court on 06.08.2019.

Sub Divisional Judge, 1969 Crl.L.J. 77 (DELHI)'observed as follows: "the plain reading of the Section would show that the real gravamen of the offence lies in the accused acting or ommitting to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge and thereby causing danger, obstruction or injury to any person in public way, etc."

sentences.text: 11. PW1 categorically deposed that accused had set up a temporary but full fleged shop using 'rehdi/rehri' on the road of IInd 60 Foota Road, Molarband Extension, Badarpur.
The Court has gone through the photographs placed on record by the IO wherein the size of shop is clearly visible.
Accused has been alleged to be the person in possession of and in charge of the said shop.
Accused has not challenged this part of the testimony of witness during his cross examination.
There is no denial of the factum of possession of the shop with accused.
As such, possession of shop with accused stands established.
12. It is observed that a shop of the size visible in photographs is certainly an obstruction to the public walking on the main road or using the road for plying vehicles.
Also, customers visiting the said shop would further cause obstruction on the public way.
Such an effect is directly attributable to the accused.
The structure being temporary and make shift is also a probable danger to public safety on a public way.
As such, the second ingredient of the offence under Section 283 IPC also stands established.
13. In view of the law discussed above and the observations of this Court, all necessary ingredients of offence under Section 283 IPC stand proved against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accused Raghvendra R. is, accordingly convicted of the offence punishable under section 283 of IPC vide Section 255 (3) of Code of Criminal Procedure.

(ARVIND BANSAL)
Announced in open Court ACMM/SOUTHEAST on 11.01.2021 DISTRICT /SAKET COURT /
